items.title: Direct Booking Tug-of-War: Hotels’ Long Bid to Take Back Power
items.summary: Ten years after Hilton, Marriott, and other chains began coaxing travelers to book directly, online travel agencies still control roughly the same slice of the pie. Yet the chains have won the economics: lower commissions, better contract terms, and stronger loyalty programs.

items.title: Accor CEO Bazin to Step Down in 2028, Shareholders Push Back on Pay
items.summary: Accor had a retirement policy. So the news here is CEO Sébastien Bazin saying a “succession search” is underway and that he may leave sooner if the board “finds the right person.” More than 40% of shareholders voted against his pay.

items.title: Expedia x IShowSpeed: Why Brands Are Doubling Down on Creators
items.summary: Expedia's IShowSpeed partnership is another signal that creator marketing has moved from experiment to core strategy among travel brands — though it’s not yet clear how its social media impressions are converting to bookings.

items.title: It Took Eight Years to Create a One-Page PDF for the U.S. Airline Industry
items.summary: America keeps building its air-travel consumer framework around disclosure, where Europe built it around liability, and two decades of evidence from across the Atlantic says our theory is wrong.

items.title: Marriott Signs ResortPass Deal. Why Hotels Are Pushing to Sell More Than Rooms.
items.summary: Hotels have long treated the room as the only thing worth selling. Marriott's deal with ResortPass signals a growing sideline to boost margins: selling empty pool chairs and spa slots to locals who show up for the day.

items.title: Mews and SiteMinder to Put Hotel Distribution, Operations Under One Roof — Exclusive
items.summary: Mews and SiteMinder are bringing distribution and hotel operations into one platform. The goal: Break down the hotel data silos that complicate AI adoption in the agentic age.

items.title: Airbnb Invests in WeRoad — and Hired Its CEO to Lead Hotels
items.summary: Airbnb has struggled to scale experiences. Investing in WeRoad — and hiring its CEO — is Chesky's preferred move: partner first, potentially acquire later.

items.title: Waldorf Astoria, Aman, and Auberge Invest in Texas Hill Country
items.summary: These may read as bets on new Texas wealth. They’re also real estate plays, with branded residential as the anchor that makes the hotels financeable.
